states: Refreshing current commits one successor verifier and records the retired verifier and rotation time.
Retrying that retired verifier inside five seconds replaces the successor; it does not extend the window or expiry.
After concurrent same-parent requests settle, exactly one returned successor matches authoritative current state. Displaced access tokens fail online verification.

Presenting a displaced refresh branch revokes the family as ORPHANED_BRANCH. Clients must serialize installation and use of their refreshed credentials; arbitrary concurrent use of both branches is not qualified.
Retired-parent replay after the window is RECENT_PREV; older ancestry is STALE_LINEAGE. Both revoke the intended family server-side before a successful theft response, preserving other families.
A database backend terminated after UPDATE but before commit must leave every rotation column unchanged and allow the original credential to retry.
A committed refresh response lost before downstream headers or truncated after eight body bytes permits window-root retry. The proof uses a real transport proxy and actual database state.
A successful response held across logout cannot resurrect the revoked server-side family when it is eventually delivered.
Legacy CDI5.4 and CDI5.6 transitions are characterized explicitly; they are not assumed to have identical retry semantics.
